question: When does Hamiltonian structure improve cross-energy prediction and control after accounting for representation, mechanics, coverage and optimization?
scope: Shared Fourier bandwidth with exact convex fits; no general deep-HNN or novelty claim
paired_sampling: Independent local/global training pools and validation pools; coverage conditions reuse prefixes and labels; global snapshots have p=0
validation_rule: Minimum noisy validation vector MSE within each family and coverage condition; ties in candidate order; no refit and no test-based selection
test_sampling: Fresh seeds independent of Phases 1-5 and all training/validation pools
true_integrator: RK4; five 0.01 substeps; no speed clipping
strict_success: Euclidean momentum error <0.25 at all final 20 states

mpc.initialization: Best of shifted previous plan and gain-2 feedback rollout under the same learned model
mpc.selection: Fixed before outcomes; no test tuning

reference_access: Known-force feedback and true-model MPC are privileged feasibility references with true-force access during control, not fair data-budget baselines or theoretical upper bounds
statistics: Paired test states; crossed SAC seeds and paired world datasets; descriptive seed variation, no IID-cell significance tests
animation_selection: World seed 10, policy seed 10 when relevant, rotation initial state index 0; no outcome-based choice
